design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that the 62 children with chronic OME were randomly divided among antibiotic, antibiotic plus intranasal budesonide, and untreated control groups, although the sequence-generation method is not described.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment was reported and measured baseline risk factors were broadly similar, but neither the method used to generate the allocation sequence nor allocation concealment was described, and there was some numerical age imbalance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients were randomly assigned to three groups, namely, antibiotic treatment (20 patients...), antibiotic treatment combined with intranasal budesonide (20 patients...), and no treatment (22 patients).

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and families would probably know whether a child received oral medication, nasal spray, or no treatment, and adherence, protocol deviations, and intention-to-treat analysis were not reported, although no specific deviation is documented.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Group 1... received only antibiotic... Group 2... received intranasal budesonide spray in addition to the same antibiotic treatment... Group 3... was followed without treatment as the control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Eight-week results account for all ears with OME at baseline in each randomized group, with denominators unchanged (37, 36, and 40 ears), and no losses to follow-up are apparent.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Resolution rates were 24% (9/37 ears), 39% (14/36), and 5% (2/40) with antibiotic, budesonide, and no treatment groups, respectively.

domain_judgments.rationale: Resolution was defined using objective tympanometry plus pneumatic otoscopy and assessed at the same scheduled times, but assessor blinding is unreported and otoscopic interpretation could be influenced by knowledge of visibly different treatment assignments.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Observation of tympanic membrane mobility on pneumatic otoscopy and a type A curve on tympanogram... was accepted as resolution of OME.

domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol or preregistration is reported, and outcomes were evaluated at two time points using both otoscopy and tympanometry, leaving possible flexibility in selecting measurements or analyses, although the reported outcomes align with the stated methods.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Otoscopic examination findings and the results of tympanograms obtained at the time of diagnosis, and at the end of four and eight weeks of treatment were evaluated.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The main limitations are absent details on sequence generation and allocation concealment, likely lack of participant blinding with no adherence/ITT information, unreported assessor blinding, and no prespecified protocol or analysis plan; outcome data nevertheless appear complete.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports block randomization using computer-generated random numbers, with sequence generation performed by an author not directly involved in treatment and allocation conducted by a resident not involved in the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Computer-generated block randomization was reported and measured baseline characteristics were broadly comparable, but the method used to conceal the allocation sequence until enrollment and assignment was not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The blocks were generated randomly by an author, who was not directly involved in treatment of patient, according to computer generated random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and caregivers necessarily knew whether they received medication or observation, and adherence and intention-to-treat analysis were not explicitly reported, although no intervention-related deviations or exclusions were described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Parent/guardian and participants of group D were counselled about the condition and its management options and were advised for observation for a month without active treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 160 randomized participants appear in the outcome table, with 40 analyzed in each of the four groups, indicating complete outcome data despite no explicit participant flow diagram.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: There were a total of 160 participants in the study divided equally into four groups, thus each group consisting of 40 children.

domain_judgments.rationale: OME improvement was objectively and uniformly classified using follow-up tympanometry, and the consultant otolaryngologists performing reassessment were reported to be unaware of study assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Children were re-evaluated with clinical examination including otoscopy and tympanometry during follow-up by consultant otolaryngologist who were not aware whether the children were subjected to study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trial was registered and the main outcome definition and analysis are described, the provided report does not establish that a prespecified protocol or statistical analysis plan fixed all outcome comparisons and analyses before unblinded data were available, and it reports further post-hoc pairwise analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Further ad-hoc analysis by Tukey method was done between each pair of groups which showed all the comparisons were statistically significant (p value <0.001 in each of all comparisons).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by insufficient information about allocation concealment, lack of explicit adherence and intention-to-treat reporting in an unblinded intervention, and uncertainty about prespecification of all reported analyses. Complete outcome data and blinded, objective tympanometric outcome assessment reduce concern in the remaining domains.

design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that participants were randomly assigned to three intervention groups, although the sequence-generation and concealment methods are not described.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although random assignment was explicitly reported and baseline characteristics were broadly similar, the method of sequence generation and allocation concealment were not described, and age differed somewhat across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomly assigned into three groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and caregivers were evidently aware of assignment because interventions differed and the control received no treatment, while adherence, treatment deviations, and the analysis population were not described; however, the objective outcome limits the likely impact.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The first group received 4 ml montelukast daily for one month, and the second group received inhaled mometasone: one puff in each side of nose for one month. The third group received no treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome counts in Table 2 sum to all 143 enrolled participants (59, 40, and 44 across groups), indicating complete outcome data at one month.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We studied 143 children in this study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Tympanometry is an appropriate objective measure and was scheduled identically across groups, but the criteria for complete versus partial improvement and whether the evaluating physician was blinded were not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All patients had undergone tympanometry at the start of study and after one month to confirm the OME and to evaluate the response to treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: A trial registration is reported, but the supplied article does not establish that registration or a prespecified analysis plan preceded the study, and the analysis of the ordinal response outcome is insufficiently detailed to rule out selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov with ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02541760.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The main limitations are absent details on sequence generation and allocation concealment, lack of information on adherence/deviations and blinding, incompletely defined outcome categories, and insufficient evidence that reported outcomes and analyses were prespecified; complete follow-up reduces concern about missing data.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that assignment to the case or control group was performed using a random number table.

domain_judgments.rationale: A random number table was used, but allocation concealment was not described, and potentially relevant baseline imbalances in age and parent-reported hearing symptoms were present despite the stated nonsignificant age comparison.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The arrangement of cases in the case or control group was performed using random number table.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was only single-blinded and the added nasal spray likely revealed allocation to participants or parents, while adherence, intervention deviations, and intention-to-treat analysis were not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: According to this hypothesis, we arranged a single blinded randomized clinical trial

domain_judgments.rationale: Fourteen of 106 enrolled children were excluded during the study, including for absence at follow-up, but exclusions were not reported by randomized group or reason, and analysis included only the 92 completers, so differential outcome missingness could materially bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During the study, 14 subjects were excluded because of the presence of the exclusion criteria. Finally we completed our data with 92 patients; 46 subjects in each group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although tympanometry was objective, blinding of the audiologist and otoscopic assessors was not reported, the research team conducted otoscopy, and the subjective symptom/hearing outcome was parent-reported in a trial where treatment allocation was likely evident, creating substantial risk of differential measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After 4 weeks, all subjects in both groups underwent a 2nd otoscopic exam and tympanometry, and any improvement or worsening of complaints was directly asked from them and/or their parents.

domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol or prespecified analysis plan is reported, and numerous outcomes, ear-specific comparisons, categorical transformations, and statistical tests were available, with emphasis on significant findings despite a nonsignificant right-ear tympanometry result, allowing selective reporting or analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For comparing the results of treatments between the two groups, we used Mann-Whitney test. According to 1st and 2nd tympanometries for each case, we considered 4 classes for the results; complete remission, partial remission, no change, and exacerbation

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by post-randomization exclusion of 14 participants without group-specific accounting, likely unblinded assessment of subjective and otoscopic outcomes, and substantial flexibility in outcome definitions and analyses without a reported prespecified protocol. Additional concerns arise from unreported allocation concealment and intervention adherence.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that participants were randomly assigned using a computer-generated table of random numbers, with the final digit determining assignment to one of two treatment groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although a computer-generated sequence was described, allocation concealment was not reported and the very large baseline age imbalance between groups raises concern that the randomization process did not produce comparable groups or may not have been implemented as intended.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A computer-generated table of random numbers was used for group assignment... The mean age of the 1st group was 4.28 1.74, while the mean age in the 2nd group was 5.91 1.62.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and caregivers were evidently aware of treatment because only one group used nasal spray, and adherence beyond supervised administration of the first dose, protocol deviations, and use of an intention-to-treat analysis were not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Proper health education was provided to the parents for proper use of nasal spray, and the first dose was given in the clinic.

domain_judgments.rationale: The follow-up tables account for all 84 randomized children in each group at two and four weeks, with cell counts summing to the full group totals and no attrition indicated.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Follow-up was done after 2 and 4 weeks clinically and by tympanometry and audiometry.

domain_judgments.rationale: Tympanometry and pure-tone audiometry are appropriate objective measures applied across groups, but outcome-assessor blinding was not reported and audiometry may involve assessor or participant influence.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Follow-up was done after 2 and 4 weeks clinically and by tympanometry and audiometry.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective registration or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, while outcomes were measured for both ears at multiple time points and could support multiple eligible analyses; reporting is also internally inconsistent regarding ears and p-values.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Chi-square test and t-test were used for comparison of tympanometric data and air-bone gap respectively. Statistical significance was chosen at 0.05.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because the substantial baseline age imbalance, together with absent reporting of allocation concealment, raises serious concerns about the randomization process. Additional concerns arise from the open-label design, unclear adherence and analysis approach, absent assessor blinding, and lack of a prespecified analysis plan.
